citation.title: Visual projection neurons in the Drosophila lobula link feature detection to distinct behavioral programs
citation.authors: Wu M, Nern A, Williamson WR, Morimoto MM, Reiser MB, Card GM, Rubin GM.

agent.question: Which visual projection neurons drive backward walking (retreat) in Drosophila, and is the moonwalker pathway necessary?

analyses.text: gt19_lplc2_activate_backward (induce backward): observed stop -> inconsistent [label inferred from brain readout, no body run] (SURPRISE - reopen assumptions)
gt08_lplc2_activate_escape (induce escape): observed escape -> consistent [label inferred from brain readout, no body run]

Real run, n_trials=2, seed 0, 500 ms, 150 Hz. (1) gt20/gt21 LC16->MDN 32 Hz: consistent (brain-readout inference; also a literature-known driver ranked 16 by the connectome prior, found after 16 guided experiments vs 163.5 random = 10.2x). (2) gt20 embodied_01 (MDN intact): bridge backward 0.216, forward_disp -1.22 mm, 3.24 mm/s, label 'stop' -> INCONSISTENT/surprise. The classifier label is likely a threshold artifact: the body moved ~1.2 mm backward, so 'stop' is arguably wrong. The brain-to-body gain is the weak link. (3) gt19 LPLC2->MDN 0 Hz: inconsistent (surprise), but gt19 is medium con

decision.text: Run cycle 2 on necessity: LC16 activation with MDN silenced vs. unsilenced, brain replicates (more seeds) plus one embodied silenced-MDN run; fix the 'stop' label ambiguity.

agent.label: Hypotheses are AGENT-GENERATED and unconfirmed in the wet lab.
